<reason>B established the decisive distinction between requiring adequate protection and requiring stronger plans. A made a persuasive general case for prevention, but repeatedly mischaracterized B’s mandatory advance assessment as reactive or incomplete. Against existing enforceable plans already covering later hours, A never established why additional strengthening was necessary; its eventual concession that reattaching plans might close no gap weakened its central comparison.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B clarified that risk-specific remedies follow comprehensive assessment, neutralizing A’s stranded-crowd example. It also directly resolved the transit-delay challenge: delaying approval to fix inadequate transport is justified, while delaying an already-safe extension for unnecessary strengthening is not.</best_rebuttal>
